text:
Alex G: quick question — planning an A/B in Console for the chat model change (model:v1 -> model:v1-quant). want to validate latency/cost tradeoffs. thinking: 10% of traffic to variant, bucketing by user_id, and an exposure guard. any objections?
Maya R: sounds reasonable. do we want sticky buckets (user_id) or request-level hashing? sticky is better for UX.
Samir K: +1 sticky by user_id. also we should reserve a QA override route for our internal users to always hit the variant. makes debugging easier.
Diana P: what metrics will the guard use? latency P95 and error rate? we should also watch token cost delta.
Alex G: yes — P95 latency, error rate (5xx), and tokens-per-response delta. guard rules proposal: stop rollout if P95 increases > 20ms OR error rate increases > 0.3% absolute OR tokens-per-response increases > 5 tokens. and require at least 2k samples before evaluating.
Lee I: suggest using relative thresholds for latency (e.g., +10%) instead of absolute ms — different endpoints have different baselines. also make min_samples=2000 and min_duration=30m so noisy spikes don't kill it.
Maya R: good point. update: guard = {"min_samples": "2000", "min_duration": "30m", "latency_threshold": "+10%", "error_rate_delta": "+0.3%", "tokens_delta": "+5"}.
Samir K: implementations detail — Console UI needs to generate the routing rule and the API payload for the router service. should the experiment object include the bucketing key and fallback model? e.g.:
```
{
  "experiment_id": "exp.chat.quant.Apr2026",
  "variants": ["model:v1","model:v1-quant"],
  "traffic_split": {"model:v1": 90, "model:v1-quant": 10},
  "bucketing_key": "user_id",
  "override_rules": {"internal_team": "model:v1-quant"}
}
```
Diana P: yep that's fine. also include a rollout_ramp config (10% -> 50% over 2h) so we can auto-increase if guards pass.
Alex G: ramp plan: start 10% for 1h, then 30% for 1h, then 50% stable. each stage must meet guard checks to proceed.
Lee I: routing note — need consistent hashing in the router so variant assignment doesn't change when we scale pods. also confirm KV cache compatibility: quantized model might have slightly different cache keys. add a compatibility check step pre-rollout.
Maya R: telemetry: wire up a per-experiment tag on traces/metrics: `experiment_id=exp.chat.quant.Apr2026`. need dashboards for P95, error_rate, tokens/response, cost_estimate. can we reuse the existing experiments dashboard skeleton?
Samir K: yes, Console has a template. I'll add a per-variant breakdown and cohort table (by country, SDK version).
Alex G: API contract note for Console -> router: we need an endpoint POST /v1/experiments that includes the JSON above plus `guard_policy` and `ramp_policy`. router returns 201 + exp_id and a validation report.
Diana P: validation report should include sample-size-projection, estimated qps, and compatibility warnings (cache mismatch, kernel mismatch).
Maya R: UX: on the Console create flow show an estimated cost delta in $/1000 requests for the chosen split and ramp. product wants dollarized impact upfront.
Lee I: ops concern — ensure per-customer quotas are respected. if a single customer is heavy and lands in variant, we should enforce their rate limits independently of experiment split (no quota evasion).
Samir K: agree. router should apply quotas after routing decision; also add a safety fallback: if variant is overloaded, route to control model.
Alex G: good. last thing — who will create the experiment in Console? Samir will create staging experiment, Maya will review metrics, Diana approves for prod. can we set the experiment visibility to `team:platform` by default?
Samir K: I'll create the staging experiment now and post the link.
DevEx Bot: experiment created (staging): exp.chat.quant.Apr2026-stg. Console link: https://console.redwood.ai/experiments/exp.chat.quant.Apr2026-stg :white_check_mark:
Alex G: thanks — once staging collects ~2k samples ping this thread and we'll run the guard eval.
Maya R: tagging @Diana P for approval when ready. :eyes:
Diana P: will review. thanks folks.
